# dsh-opencode-session-fix

> Tested on DSH Desktop **0.2.1-rc.5** (Windows 11, Node 26.12.1), profile bundle
> `@deepseek-ai/ds

h-experimental-auto-review` + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`,
> provider `opencode-go`.
>
> 中文文档：READM

imental-auto-review` + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`,
> provider `opencode-go`.
>
> 中文文档：README.zh.md

> **Fixed upstream in DSH 0.2.2.** This plugin exists only as a patch for older
> releases (0.2.1-rc

.5 and earlier). It is not maintained against newer

A Host-only plugin for DeepSeek Harness that repairs one specific failure: with
the **Auto review**

permission preset (`EXP`) and an opencode family provider as
the current model, every reviewed tool
call fails before its body runs:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin supplies a session id for opencode requests that arrive without one,
so the pi-ai provide

r can emit the `x-opencode-session` header. Requests that
already carry a session id — the main conv
ersation — are untouched.
## Root cause
| Step | Where | Detail |
| Auto review builds its request | `dsh-experimental-auto-review/lib/index.js` (`classifyRisk`) | fr
ozen `{ provider, model, system, messages, temperature, signal }` — **no `sessionId`**, then `ctx.ll

m.stream(options)` |
| Main agent builds its request | `dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js` | the same call

**with** `sessionId: this.session.id` |
| Dispatch | `dsh-llm/lib/index.js` | `stream()` → `llm/str
eam` waterfall → `adapterStream()` → `registration.adapter.prepareCall()` → that call's `stream(prep

aredOptions)` |
| Header construction | `dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js` | `...options.sessionId === und

efined ? {} : { sessionId: String(options.sessionId) }` |
| Header injection | `@earendil-works/pi-a
i/dist/providers/opencode-headers.js` | `if (!options?.sessionId) return options` — no session id me
s/opencode-headers.js` | `if (!options?.sessionId) return options` — no session id means no header |

So the reviewer request reaches opencode without the routing header and is
rejected with `400 Missin

gSessionID`. Nothing is wrong with the provider
configuration.
## Why this seam

- The `llm/stream` waterfall cannot rewrite the request: its listener signature
is `(options, next)`

and `next` takes no arguments, so a listener can only
wrap the stream that the adapter has already

been handed.
- Re-registering the provider is refused with `DUPLICATE_ADAPTER`, and rewriting
the pr

ovider's static `headers` would collapse the main conversation into the
reviewer's bucket.
- Every d

ispatch path — `llm.stream()` and a prepared call — goes through the
object returned by the register

ed adapter's `prepareCall()`. That object, plus
the adapter's own `stream()`, is what this plugin wr

dapter's `prepareCall()`. That object, plus
the adapter's own `stream()`, is what this plugin wraps.

**Wrap `prepareCall()`, not just `stream()`.** In 0.2.1-rc.5 pi-ai's
`prepareCall()` returns `{ mode

l, stream }` whose `stream` closes over its own
snapshot and never calls the instance `stream()` met

tream }` whose `stream` closes over its own
snapshot and never calls the instance `stream()` method:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Wrapping only `stream()` therefore leaves the reviewer path unfixed. The test
suite in `test/wrapper
.test.mjs` reproduces exactly this adapter shape.
## Behaviour

- Provider routes: `opencode-go` and `opencode` by default; configurable.
- Missing or blank `sessio

nId` → a stable id is injected
(`dsh-opencode-session-<uuid>`, one per activation, or `config.sessio

nId`).
- Existing `sessionId` → forwarded unchanged, so the main conversation keeps its
real session

id and its own routing bucket.
- Other providers served by the same adapter instance → untouched, b

ecause every
request is filtered by `options.provider`.
- A frozen request (Auto review deep-freezes

its request) is copied, never
mutated.
- On `llm/adapters-updated` the patch is moved to the newly

built adapter; when
the plugin unloads, every wrapped method is restored (inherited methods are
dele

ted again, not shadowed).
- If `llm.adapters` is not a `Map`, the plugin warns once and does nothing
instead of failing profile activation.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Swap `web` for your profile name; the dump should contain
`- id: opencode-session-fix`. The package

is published to npm, so it is also
available in the in-app plugin center.

Desktop: the `desktop` profile is owned by the Electron shell and the CLI
refuses it. Use **Settings

→ Plugins → install** with the package name
`dsh-opencode-session-fix`, or with this repository's U

Plugins → install** with the package name
`dsh-opencode-session-fix`, or with this repository's URL.

Source install without npm:
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:imx123/dsh-opencode-session-fix`, o

r a local
checkout path.
## Configuration

Override the inserted row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the override
replaces the whole `conf

ide the inserted row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the override
replaces the whole `config`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Real device: enable Auto review (`EXP`), select an `opencode-go` model, let a
`write` be reviewed. T
he session log shows the gate that decides it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

and that reviewed `write` returned normally instead of
`auto-review of tool "write" failed ... 400 M

`write` returned normally instead of
`auto-review of tool "write" failed ... 400 MissingSessionID`.

Regression: the main conversation's `x-opencode-session` must still equal the
real session id (not t

he plugin's id). Uninstalling the plugin must bring the
`400` back — the patch is reversible.
## Risk and scope

Process-local only: no network calls of its own, no credentials, no disk writes,
no session events.

The plugin wraps one object inside the running Host and
restores it when unloaded, so the only thing

it can influence is the
`x-opencode-session` header of the configured provider routes.
This is a community plugin, not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.
